editorial:
Imagine being stuck at a music camp in a giant, creepy mansion where the walls feel like they are watching you. That is exactly where you find Flea, a kid who would rather play pranks and scare his classmates than practice his instruments. The vibe of the movie is a fun mix of a childhood summer camp story and a spooky mystery. You get to follow Flea as he tries to be the biggest prankster in the house, but he soon finds out that the mansion might actually have some real secrets that are way scarier than his little jokes.

What really works here is the pacing and the way the tension builds up. The acting feels natural, and you can really relate to that feeling of being a bored kid looking for trouble. While some of the special effects feel a bit old, they actually add to the charm of the film. If you love stories about kids discovering things they aren't supposed to, you will enjoy this one. You should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Flea realizes that the ghosts in the mansion are not just tricks of the mind. After his pranks go too far, he has to face the actual spirits of the house. He eventually learns how to stop the haunting by making peace with the ghosts' past. Everything wraps up with Flea finally respecting the music and the house, leaving the mansion as a changed person who understands that some things are better left alone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves nostalgic ghost stories and coming-of-age tales.
